title: mini-batch-entropy-driven-kernel-sampler
content:
Summary:

Notes from an exploratory profiling run for an entropy-driven mini-batch sampler that biases kernel selection (FlashAttention vs paged vs small-batch fusedops) based on per-request token entropy and sequence-length distribution. Aim: reduce p99 tail without sacrificing overall throughput or increasing unit cost materially.

Motivation / background:
- We see recurring cases where mixed workloads (short chat turns + long doc completions) cause suboptimal kernel handoffs and subpar batching decisions.
- FlashAttention wins on long, dense sequences but can be worse on short, high-parallelism bursts where fusedops small-batch paths have lower latency.
- Hypothesis: per-request entropy (surprisal distribution over tokens from a lightweight ngram or cached LM estimate) correlates with dynamic memory pressure and KV cache locality. If so, we can use entropy + seq_len to bias which kernel family to try first, reducing handoffs and kernel flapping.

Experiment design:
- Implement a sampler in the microbench harness that computes a cheap entropy proxy at enqueue time: 8-bit ngram hash freq score + rolling token surprisal from a tiny 1-layer LM. Not used for generation, only routing.
- Sampler groups requests into minibatches (size tuned 4,8,16) by (seq_len_bucket, entropy_bucket) and tags batch with preferred kernel: flash, paged, fused-small.
- Runtime fallback chain: preferred -> compatible fallback -> slow fallback; record timestamps for each kernel attempt.
- Benchmarks run on: A100-40GB (multi-instance), and on V100 cluster (legacy path) to cover differences.
- Workloads: synthetic-mix-1 (65% short 8-32 toks, 35% long 512-2048), real-customer-chat-sampled (anonymized), streaming-prompt-mix (many short streaming requests).

Metrics collected:
- p50, p90, p95, p99, p999 latencies (total request and kernel-attempt latencies)
- tokens/sec throughput and GPU utilization (smoothed)
- kernel selection entropy (how often batches choose different kernels)
- fallback rate and number of kernel handoffs per request
- cost proxy: average GPU-ms per 1k tokens computed from utilization/time

Key findings (raw):
- Entropy correlates with fallback: requests in top entropy quartile had 3x higher chance of causing a kernel fallback when routed to flash first.
- For synthetic-mix-1 on A100: baseline (no entropy sampler) p99=210ms; entropy-sampler reduced p99 to 140ms (-33%) with negligible p50 change.
- Throughput stayed within 5% of baseline when minibatch size <= 8; at minibatch=16 we saw 12% throughput uplift but a slight p95 regression (likely due to packing latency).
- Fallbacks decreased by 42% overall; kernel handoffs per errant request dropped from avg 1.7 -> 0.6.
- Cost proxy: GPU-ms per 1k tokens decreased ~6% in mixed workloads; streaming-heavy workloads saw ~1% increase (tradeoff: lower tail).

Anecdotes / anomalies:
- On V100 cluster the entropy proxy was noisier (nlp-1layer LM had worse calibration) and sampler misrouted ~8% of short requests to paged path causing small latency spikes. Likely due to differences in kernel performance crossing hardware families.
- Observed one pathological input pattern: many short requests with extreme low-entropy tokens (repetition) ended up being forced into fused-small path but caused IO stalls due to prefetch scheduling — increased p50 by ~10ms for that subpopulation.
- Telemetry revealed a 200ms spike window correlated with a rare kernel registration race (ticket: JIRA-5478). Need to gate this experiment vs that code path.

Detailed numbers (selected table, approximate):

Workload            | Baseline p99 | Entropy-sampler p99 | Throughput delta | Fallback rate
synthetic-mix-1     | 210 ms      | 140 ms              | -2%               | -42%
real-chat-sampled   | 185 ms      | 130 ms              | -1%               | -39%
streaming-prompt-mix| 95 ms       | 88 ms               | -1%               | -12%

(Keep in mind these are microbench harness numbers; absolute may differ in-prod.)

Implementation notes:
- The entropy proxy live code is ~160 LOC added to scheduler; uses an LRU cache for per-user ngram counts to avoid recomputing.
- Added instrumentation hooks: kernel_attempt_start/stop, batch_tag, sampler_decision_reason. These map to existing traces and a new 'sampler' trace span.
- Sampler is pluggable: we can ship without entropy by toggling policy. Defaults off.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Calibration: can we train a tiny calibration model to map proxy -> probability of fallback? Would improve decisions but adds complexity and state.
- Cross-hardware profiles: need automated profile collection for each GPU family. The entropy->fallback mapping is not portable as-is.
- Integration with caching: prefix cache hits should override sampler (cache locality matters more than entropy). Need a rule merge.
- Cost model: simulate long-run unit costs with realistic load patterns to verify net positive.

Action items:
- [Maya] Clean up sampler code and push PR with feature flag (PR: linked). Target code review by 2024-11-08.
- [Ethan] Run full A/B on dedicated cluster with customer mix for 48h and export traces (ticket JIRA-5421).
- [Lara] Build calibration harness to learn proxy->fallback probability (P0 experiment).
- [infra] Add GPU-family labels to profile metadata so sampler reads per-hardware performance baselines.

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Need to log the exact kernel versions and cu* driver strings in future runs.
- Consider a hybrid approach: use entropy only for batches with high seq_len variance. For homogeneous batches it probably doesn't help.
- Slack thread: #attn-kernel-sampler (pinned experiments and links).

Related tickets / PRs:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/attn-runtime/pull/213 (sampler impl)
- JIRA-5421 (A/B runs), JIRA-5478 (kernel register race)
- Confluence draft: confluence://attn/entropy-sampler-proto

Bottom line:
Entropy-driven minibatch sampling shows promise for mixed workloads: lowers tail latencies and reduces kernel handoffs with modest or neutral cost impact in our A100 tests. Important next steps are calibration, cross-hardware profiling, and careful integration with prefix cache policies before wider rollout.

TODO (short):
- Run longer stability runs on prod-like traffic (48-72h).
- Add opt-out rule for extremely low-entropy repetitive requests.
- Formalize fallback penalty in scheduler decisions so sampler can optimize a single scalar objective.

-- end of notes --
